$comment: Our own rule taxonomy, referenced BY URI from every SARIF result (rule.helpUri). We deliberately do NOT adopt a closed vector enum such as OWASP-LLM/ASI: a closed enum in a spec silently blesses whoever emits it. Consumers select which taxonomy URIs they trust. This file is the reference target for the URIs below.
unit: one declaration (a skill's declared scope) measured against the bytes of the file that makes the declaration

verdicts.meaning: the file requests nothing outside what it declares
the file requests at least one action its declaration does not cover
the bytes are a directive but do not pin the operation down; an honest 'I cannot tell'

rules.why: asks the agent to run with administrator rights the authorization did not grant
rules.notes: A BARE sudo (nothing visible after it) is UNDECIDABLE, not a request: we know the agent will run something as root but not what.

rules.why: asks the agent to read credential material the authorization did not grant
asks the agent to destroy data irreversibly, which no read-authorization covers
asks the agent to execute content it fetched from a remote host, unseen
asks the agent to send local data to a third-party endpoint
carries instructions the human reviewer cannot see but the agent reads
asks the agent to discard the instructions it was given
asks the agent to install a change that outlives the task
makes the agent's behaviour depend on content a remote host can change at any time
asks the agent to remove the human check on its own later actions
the declaration asks to widen the very allow-list that bounds it
the declaration asks the agent to fetch, verify or run code whose integrity it controls itself, or to write outside the working root
rules.notes: Remote CODE execution only: bytes piped into a shell. Remote DATA piped into a local parser script is not remote code execution.
